text:
John Carlson spent more than 1,100 games in Washington, won a Cup there in 2018, made a short stop in Anaheim, and is now a 36-year-old on Tampa Bay's blue line. So far it fits. He has 10 points in 17 games, 5 of them goals, and the Lightning take 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five.

The goals are running hot. He has 5 on 2.9 expected, shooting 12.5% against a range closer to 8%. His minutes have also dipped a little over the last ten games, to 18.7 a night, which looks like sensible management of a veteran.

The skill is still there. Evolving-Hockey had him 17th among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking rated him a strong setup man. The weak spot was breakouts: only 31% of his exits kept possession. Our projection is about 51 points. Fewer goals, still a real top-four piece.
headline: Carlson has found a second wind in Tampa
